title: openai-compat: tool calling schema mapping + tool_choice semantics + message formatting fixes
author: Ava Chen
description: Add comprehensive OpenAI-compatibility layer updates for function/tool calling: canonicalize tool schema mapping, implement tool_choice semantics for explicit tool selection, and stabilize tool message formatting for streaming and structured output. This PR fixes several interoperability gaps observed with downstream SDKs and external integrations; introduces a deterministic mapping layer between Redwood tool descriptors and OpenAI-style tool schemas; updates runtime handling so tool_choice signals cause immediate tool invocation without ambiguous assistant messages; and ensures streamed tool outputs preserve JSON framing and content-type hints for downstream parsers. Includes unit and integration tests, docs updates, and migration notes for existing tool authors.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add schema mapper from redwood tool descriptors to OpenAI tool schemas
fix(openai-compat): preserve content-type hints during streaming tool responses
feat(runtime): add tool_choice handling path that short-circuits assistant message emission
test(openai-compat): add e2e tests for tool_choice + schema mapping
docs: document tool schema mapping and message formatting expectations
ci_summary: CI: linux-build passed, unit-tests passed, integration-tests flakey on first run (timeout on streaming e2e) then rerun succeeded, lint fixed automatically by prettier, coverage 91%
review_thread: Marcus: Can you explain how schema mapping handles nested object refs? Author: The mapper flattens OpenAPI-like $ref into inline schemas by default and preserves original ref as metadata; see mapper.ts for algorithm sketch. Diego: tool_choice path needs to be sync to prevent double assistant messages; requested a test that asserts no assistant payload is emitted when tool_choice is present. Author: Added e2e assertion and runtime guard that short-circuits assistant emission. Sofia: Docs should call out migrating custom tools that relied on legacy assistant signals; requested migration notes. Author: Added migration section to docs and a compatibility flag 'allow_legacy_tool_emission' for one release cycle. Final: Approved by Marcus and Sofia after CI green and tests added.
release_notes: - Added OpenAI-compatible tool schema mapping to redwood-openai-compat; - Implemented tool_choice semantics so explicit tool selections invoke tools without extraneous assistant messages; - Stabilized streaming tool message formatting and preserved content-type hints for downstream consumers; - Docs: migration notes for custom tool authors and examples for structured output;
tests_added: unit tests for mapper.ts and streaming formatter; integration e2e covering tool_choice + streaming structured output
motivation: Customers integrating with OpenAI-compatible clients observed inconsistent behavior when tools returned streamed JSON and when tool_choice selection was used by models. This PR aligns Redwood's compatibility layer with OpenAI semantics to reduce integration friction.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated behind env REDWOOD_OPENAI_COMPAT=1 by default for the next minor release; enable feature in Dedicated deployments after rolling canary. Watch for increased error logs from legacy tools during migration and provide 'allow_legacy_tool_emission' toggle if requested.
